name: Bangla Road
naming_note: Bangla Road is the standard English name; it is also commonly called Soi Bangla.

facts.text: Bangla Road is a street in Patong, on Phuket Island.
Bangla Road is known for its concentration of bars, nightclubs and live-entertainment venues.
The name is also rendered in Thai transliteration as Thanon Bangla; thanon means “road.”

name: Waseda University
naming_note: Use “Waseda University” in English; its Japanese name is 早稲田大学 (Waseda Daigaku).

facts.text: Waseda University is a private university in Tokyo, Japan.
It was founded in 1882 by Ōkuma Shigenobu as Tokyo Senmon Gakkō.
The institution adopted the name Waseda University in 1902.
Its main campus is in the Waseda district of Shinjuku, Tokyo.
The Ōkuma Auditorium, a landmark campus building, was completed in 1927.

itinerary.tour: Route G: Time Travel to Good Old Tokyo

name: Myanmar–Thailand border
naming_note: For an international audience, “Myanmar–Thailand border” is clear; the itinerary refers to a northern section near Doi Chang Mub, not the whole boundary.

facts.text: It is the international boundary separating Myanmar and Thailand.
The boundary is about 2,400 kilometres long.
Its northern end meets the Mekong River at the tripoint of Thailand, Myanmar and Laos.
Mountainous terrain and river sections, including parts along the Moei and Salween rivers, form stretches of the boundary.

itinerary.sentence: Thai-Myanmar border — cycle along a road that runs beside

name: Kruba Srivichai Monument
naming_note: The monument is commonly named for Kruba Srivichai; the itinerary’s “Sri Vichai” is a spelling variant.

facts.text: The monument features a statue of Kruba Srivichai, a revered Buddhist monk associated with northern Thailand’s Lanna tradition.
It stands at the foot of Doi Suthep, beside Huay Kaew Road in Chiang Mai.
Kruba Srivichai (1878–1938) is remembered for leading the volunteer construction of the road to Wat Phra That Doi Suthep, completed in 1935.
The monument commemorates Kruba Srivichai’s religious and community work in northern Thailand.

itinerary.sentence: Kruba Sri Vichai Statue — take part in the daily Buddhist ceremony Tak Bat (Merit Making)
Kruba Sri Vichai Statue — give offerings to monks on their alms-rounds

name: Knuckles Mountain
naming_note: Use “Knuckles Mountain” for the peak; “Knuckles” also commonly refers to the wider mountain range.

facts.text: Knuckles Mountain is a peak in the Knuckles Mountain Range of central Sri Lanka.
The mountain lies within the Knuckles Conservation Forest, part of the Central Highlands of Sri Lanka UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The Knuckles Mountain Range spans parts of Kandy and Matale districts in Central Province.
The name “Knuckles” refers to the range’s resemblance to the knuckles of a clenched fist.

itinerary.tour: 6-Day Knuckles to Ella Trekking Tour in Sri Lanka

name: Baguio Cathedral
naming_note: Baguio Cathedral is the common English name; its full name is Our Lady of Atonement Cathedral.

facts.text: Baguio Cathedral is a Roman Catholic cathedral dedicated to Our Lady of Atonement.
Construction of the present cathedral began in 1920, and it was completed in 1936.
The cathedral stands on a hill in central Baguio.
Its pink exterior, twin spires and rose windows are prominent architectural features.

name: Jampa Lhakhang
naming_note: Jambay Lhakhang is the common English spelling; Jamba Lhakhang and Jampa Lhakhang are also used.

facts.text: Jambay Lhakhang is a Buddhist temple dedicated to Jampa, the future Buddha, also known as Maitreya.
According to Bhutanese tradition, Tibetan king Songtsen Gampo founded the temple in the 7th century as one of 108 temples built to subdue a demoness.
The temple stands in the Chamkhar Valley in Bumthang.
The annual Jambay Lhakhang Drup, also known as Bumthang Drup, is held at the temple.

itinerary.sentence: Jambay Lhakhang Festival — spend the morning at

name: Plains of Bangladesh
naming_note: This is a broad geographic description rather than a single formally bounded site; “the plains of Bangladesh” is clear for an international audience.

facts.text: The plains are a broad lowland region covering much of Bangladesh.
Much of the region lies within the Ganges–Brahmaputra–Meghna delta.
Its alluvial soils were deposited by the Ganges, Brahmaputra, Meghna and their tributaries.
The landscape is generally flat and crossed by many rivers, distributaries and wetlands.
Monsoon rains and seasonal river flooding shape large parts of the plains.

itinerary.sentence: plains of Bangladesh — come into view

name: Karkyra Base Camp
naming_note: For an international audience, use “Karkyra Base Camp” in Kyrgyzstan; the valley and camp name are also commonly spelled “Karkara.”

facts.text: Karkyra Base Camp is a mountain camp in the Karkyra Valley of eastern Kyrgyzstan.
The camp lies in Issyk-Kul Region, near the Kazakhstan–Kyrgyzstan border.
The Karkyra Valley is part of the Tian Shan mountain region.
English-language sources also render the valley’s name as Karkara.

itinerary.tour: Cultural tour to Kyrgyzstan, China and Kazakhstan
Cultural tour to Kyrgyzstan, China and Kazakhstan

name: Arkhangai Province
naming_note: Arkhangai Province is commonly called Arkhangai Aimag; “aimag” is the Mongolian term for province.

facts.text: Arkhangai is a province in north-central Mongolia.
The Khangai Mountains cover a substantial part of the province, alongside grasslands and river valleys.
Khorgo volcano and Terkhiin Tsagaan Lake are in Arkhangai, within Khorgo-Terkhiin Tsagaan Nuur National Park.
The Chuluut River flows through the province and has carved a basalt gorge.

name: Yongdusan Park
naming_note: Yongdusan Park is the established English name; Yongdu-san Park is a spelling variant.

facts.text: Yongdusan Park is an urban park on Yongdusan, a hill in central Busan.
The name Yongdusan means “Dragon Head Mountain.”
More than 70 types of trees grow in the park.
A statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin is located in the park.

name: Shrine of Shah Shams Tabrez
naming_note: For international audiences, the site is commonly called the Shrine of Shah Shams Sabzwari or Shah Shams Tabrez; it is distinct from the shrine of Shams of Tabriz in Iran.

facts.text: The shrine is the mausoleum associated with the Sufi figure and Ismaili missionary Shah Shamsuddin Sabzwari.
The brick mausoleum is decorated with glazed tilework.

name: A Lưới
naming_note: A Luoi is commonly written without Vietnamese diacritics; the Vietnamese spelling is A Lưới, and the name has also referred to the wider surrounding district.

facts.text: A Luoi is a highland settlement in western Hue.
The settlement lies in the Annamite Range, near the border with Laos.
The surrounding A Shau Valley formed part of the Ho Chi Minh Trail network during the Vietnam War.

itinerary.sentence: A Luoi — cycle to and stay overnight

name: Mweka Gate
naming_note: Mweka Gate is the usual English name; “Mweka Park Gate” is also used.

facts.text: Mweka Gate is a gate of Kilimanjaro National Park.
The gate is on the southern slopes of Mount Kilimanjaro.
It lies at approximately 1,640 metres above sea level.
Kilimanjaro National Park was established in 1973.

name: Angkor Wat
naming_note: Use Angkor Wat for the temple complex itself; Angkor refers to the wider archaeological region.

facts.text: Angkor Wat was built in the first half of the 12th century under Khmer king Suryavarman II.
It was originally dedicated to the Hindu god Vishnu and later became a Buddhist religious site.
The temple complex is enclosed by a rectangular moat and galleries, with five towers at its centre.
Its gallery bas-reliefs depict scenes from Hindu epics and Khmer history.
Angkor Wat lies within the Angkor Archaeological Park in northern Cambodia.

name: Ssangyong Cave
naming_note: For an international audience, use “Ssangyong Cave”; “Sangyong Cave” is a spelling variant of the Korean name 쌍용굴.

facts.text: Ssangyong Cave is a volcanic lava tube on Jeju Island.
Its Korean name, 쌍용굴, is commonly translated as “Two-Dragon Cave.”

name: Ghurchi Lagna Pass
naming_note: Ghurchi Lagna Pass is a clear English name; the pass is also spelled Gurchi Lagna.

facts.text: Ghurchi Lagna is a mountain pass in western Nepal.
The pass lies in the Himalayan highlands of Mugu District.
Its elevation is given as about 3,480 metres.
The pass is in Karnali Province.

name: Listvyanka Market
naming_note: “Listvyanka Market” is an informal name for the market area in Listvyanka, also often called the fish market.

facts.text: It is a cluster of market stalls in Listvyanka rather than a single historic market building.
The market is associated with smoked fish from the Lake Baikal region, including omul.
Stalls also offer regional food products, souvenirs and crafts.
The market is in Listvyanka, a settlement on the western shore of Lake Baikal.

name: Fourth Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge
naming_note: For an international audience, use the common name Fourth Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge; it spans the border between Laos and Thailand.

facts.text: It is a road bridge across the Mekong River linking Huay Xai in Laos with Chiang Khong in Thailand.
It is the fourth bridge built under the Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge programme.
The bridge opened in December 2013.
The Mekong River forms the international boundary at the bridge.

name: Panfilov Park
naming_note: In Almaty, it is also commonly called the Park of 28 Panfilov Guardsmen; the itinerary also names a separate Panfilov Park in Bishkek.

facts.text: Panfilov Park is a public urban park in central Almaty.
The park’s origins date to 1870, when it was laid out as a city garden in Verny, the predecessor of Almaty.
It is named for the 28 Panfilov Guardsmen, commemorated in Soviet accounts for their defense near Moscow in 1941.
The Ascension Cathedral, also known as Zenkov Cathedral, stands within the park.
The park contains a memorial to the Second World War with an eternal flame.
The Museum of Folk Musical Instruments is located within the park.
